conclusions: Actual complete symmetric zero-diagonal A with limsup ||A||op/sqrt(n)<=5/3 and limsup tr|A|/n^(3/2)<=4/5 satisfies liminf Phi(A)/n^(3/2)>=35/88+3/1250=2/5+7/55000. No full spectral-law or diagonal-homogeneity hypothesis.

Adaptive clipped Boolean updates operate on the SAME actual nuclear-baseline phase. Uniform higher-chaos pairing and joint two-variable Gaussianization justify the heterogeneous convex-perspective gain; no all-field joint CLT or unproved square-payoff uniform integrability is used.

For ACTUAL K=[[A,B],[B^T,-A]] and any positive DIAGONAL D=diag(D_L,D_R) with D+/-K>=0, retain delta=tr(D)tr(D^(-1))/(2n)^2-1->0. With W=D_L^(-1/2) B D_R^(-1/2), Y=WW^T, the full moments are m_D=tr(Y)/n and Delta_D=tr[Y(I-Y)]/n.

If every accumulation point (m,Delta) lies in 9/25<=m<=1/2, 0<=Delta<=m[4sqrt(m)-3sqrt(1-m)]^2/25, a common large original principal source gives both certified caps and transfers the same strict lower to Phi(A)/n^(3/2). A sufficient rectangle is liminf m_D>=2/5 and limsup Delta_D<=1/1600, retaining delta->0.

The transfer uses a finite noncommuting Schatten bound and completeness to recover scale. No full cross or internal law, separate trace cap, diagonal optimality or active-state condition is assumed. The endpoint-law theorem is retained as the zero-defect case.

The region is sufficient, not necessary for exclusion. The older near-flat theorem retains its stronger gap under narrower hypotheses. Earlier formal certificates retain their listed relaxation scope; no actual counterexample was supplied there.
